transcript: People who wait so long to talk about their feelings, only to find out that all they can say is, I don't know, are experiencing what psychology calls alexithymia. But in the old temples, we would describe it differently. We would say the qi is not flowing. In traditional Chinese medicine, emotions are energy, anger rises, grief sinks, fear tightens. When you suppress them for years, the energy has nowhere to go, so it settles in the body. The chest feels heavy, the throat feels blocked, the stomach feels tight. When someone asks, what are you feeling? The answer becomes, I don't know. Not because the heart is empty, but because the river inside has been frozen for too long. Monks do not force expression. They breathe, they sit in stillness, they allow warmth to return to the body. When the energy begins to move again, words come naturally. Sometimes silence is not confusion, it is emotion waiting for a safe place to flow. If this helped you understand yourself, save this video and share it with someone who always says, I don't know how I feel. It might give them the words they've been searching for.
